verdict_d: RED: the amplitude layer is a rigid 15-point discrete spectrum with quantum 1/15 = 1/(N_gen*F_5); there is no continuous amplitude to recover, and the only continuous quantities are exact counting rationals

claims.name: C1 takes exactly 15 signed values whose magnitudes are exactly the docs/45 B2 set {0, 1/15, 2/15, 1/5, 4/15, 1/3, 2/3, 1} (the denominator 15 = N_gen * F_5 = 3 * 5 is the LCM of the reduced denominators)

the 1/15 quantum is structural, not fitted: the 120 states collapse to 60 Z2-classes (K[-s] = K[s]), so every numerator is 2*(sum over 60 classes), and that 60-term sum is always a multiple of 4 -- hence every numerator is a multiple of 8 and every correlation is a multiple of 8/120 = 1/15. The smallest positive value is exactly 1/15
claims.detail: all numerators divisible by 8 : True ; all (numerator/2) divisible by 4 : True ; smallest positive numerator = 8 (= 8/120 = 1/15)

claims.name: the full discrete spectrum of the frozen 2-party correlation (value -> number of axis pairs, 3844 total) is reported; it is a rigid 15-point spectrum, not a continuum

the reduced denominators that occur are exactly the divisors of 15 (1, 3, 5, 15): the frozen correlator has resolution 1/15 = 1/(N_gen*F_5) and no finer structure is present in ANY of the 7440 readout entries

the budget layer is a COUNTING layer, not an amplitude layer: budget 123/2, per-read cost 123/88 = 2*E_min, so exactly 44 = N_d reads per pass, and the memo-saturation tuple needs 1922/11 = 174.7273x the budget. These are exact rationals (no free parameter), so they cannot be dialled to an amplitude in [0.0211, 0.0387]
the persistent-ledger E2 correlation has the same 15-point magnitude structure (reported for the record); no entry of either table carries amplitude information beyond this discrete spectrum

mechanism audit: the FULL left-invariance kernel of the readout is {1, -1} (order 2 only) -- so the divisibility by 8 is NOT produced by a subgroup of order 4/8/10 acting trivially on the readout (that hypothesis is refuted, orders present = {1,2}); the Z2 collapse is the only invariance. The 62 axes contain 31 antipodal pairs, so the divisibility cannot come from the axes either (it must come from the group)
claims.detail: |left-invariance kernel| = 2 with element-orders [1, 2] ; antipodal unordered pairs among the 62 axes = 31

claims.name: random-generic-axis control (300 draws): for random rational integer directions (two per draw) and a random frozen h, the 120-state numerator 2*(#same - #diff) over the 60 Z2-orbits is divisible by 8 in EVERY draw. The NULL control shows the property is not automatic: an arbitrary +-1 function on the same 60 orbits fails the mod-4 parity in about half of 300 draws. Therefore the 1/15 quantum is FORCED by the +-1 sign readout on the discrete 2I orbit, not by the particular 62 frozen axis directions
claims.detail: draws with a failing parity = 0 / 300 (fixed-point-free Z2 pairing, 60 orbits) ; NULL control failures = 154 / 300

claims.name: CONTINUOUS control: replacing the +-1 binarisation by the exact inner product <u_a, R_g n_0> widens the readout value set from 2 to 11 exact values in Q(sqrt5) -- the continuum is destroyed by the SIGN MAP, not by the group (the readout map is the only lossy step)
claims.detail: un-binarised readout distinct values = 11 ; frozen readout alphabet = 2
